segments.text: Are you familiar with what's called a boreal forest?
A boreal, no, only in those countries.
In the northernmost part of the world, just below the Arctic and North America and Eurasia,
millions of acres burn there naturally every year.
Wildfires in the boreal forest in North America and Eurasia in one year, 2021,
will release double the amount of all global CO2 produced in 2001.
And three times as much as the Inflation Reduction Act is projected to reduce by 2030.
My point is, Inflation Reduction Act is going to end up costing about $1.2 trillion.
Presumably, there are estimates about how much carbon it will reduce by 2030.
American people are going to spend a lot of money, $1.2 trillion for what?
The carbon released by naturally occurring boreal forest fires in 2001 is three times the amount will save
by asking the American people to spend $1.2 trillion of their money on the Inflation Reduction Act.
Now, you know, unless you're the reason that your parents drink, that doesn't make sense, does it?
So, thank you. I mean, it's a trenchant question, Senator.
I think it's a bit of a distraction from the real issue because we take for granted...
So peer-reviewed studies, Congress?
No, and the peer-reviewed studies show...
Boreal forest fires exist, I promise you.
Oh, no, but I'm not doubting the science for one minute.
I'm saying let's take the science for granted, let's take nature for granted,
the industrial livestock practices.
My point is, I'm going way over this last question.
We spend all this money.
Okay, it's going to cost America about a trillion dollars a year to make us carbon neutral by 2050.
Yes.
We don't lower world temperatures a centile of a degree if you look at the boreal forest fires.
So what do we do?
Oh, I got you.
But would you dispute that it would be far worse if we do nothing?
In other words, if we stay on the path that big oil would have a stay on,
are you denying that we would be in a situation where the Earth's temperature goes up?
But that's not your goal.
That's not your goal in trying to make us carbon neutral is to be...
It's a zero-sum game.
Your goal is not to make it better.
Your point is, as I understand it, that the world will end if we don't achieve the carbon neutrality.
Right.
We want to prevent calamity.
We want to make our one planetary habitat as livable as possible.
Right?
Do we need to spend trillions of dollars fighting the boreal forest fires?
Well, let's go back to the Inflation Reduction Act which you invoked before.
Most of the money which you're describing as being spent on climate change measures
was actually tax incentives for the stimulation of renewable energy.
Agree, but they're not stopping the boreal forest fires.
I mean, we spend all this money and we reduce carbon
and the boreal forest fires just spit out three times the amount of carbon.
Do you...
I would love to read a peer-reviewed study on that.
I mean, if we need a boreal forest...
Economist's Magazine, they talk about it all the time.
All right.
I will check that out.
But I mean, is the suggestion that we need a boreal forest fire department?
I'm asking you.
I mean, what y'all's position is, I get it.
Nobody's perfect.
Oil and gas is bad and they're destroying the world.
Let's get rid of them.
Yeah.
Okay.
If we do that, that's going to cost a lot.
If we do that, is the world going to be okay?
No.
I got you.
I see where you're going.
But let's...
If I might...
I'm sorry, Mr. Chairman.
If I could just take your beautiful state, which is very close to my heart.
I lived in New Orleans a couple of times.
Come back and spend money.
But I definitely will.
I plan to do that.
Louisiana has traditionally dealt with hurricanes, but is now experiencing hurricanes of much greater
velocity and much greater ferocity under the climate change conditions.
Really?
Well, then again, then perhaps the science that I've been seeing...
The damages are higher because Louisiana's wealthier and there's more to destroy.
If you look at the studies on the intensity, they're about to sign.
All right.
Kennedy, Senator Cain is waiting to proceed.
I'm sorry.
We were just having a good talk.
No, I'm enjoying this.
There you are.
I'm not complaining.
I'm sorry, Jimmy.
I'm sorry.
Thank you, Congressman.
